seo.description: Discover Place Oulad Tedrarag in Laâyoune, linked to the historic Oulad Tidrarin Sahrawi tribe – a local square and neighbourhood that reflects the living heritage of the Moroccan Sahara.

name: Place Oulad Tedrarag
hero_subtitle: A local square and neighbourhood linked to the historic Oulad Tidrarin (Oulad Tedrarag) Sahrawi tribe – everyday life and deep roots in the capital of the Moroccan Sahara.

overview.title: Living Heritage of the Oulad Tidrarin
overview.p1: Place Oulad Tedrarag (associated with the Oulad Tidrarin / Oulad Tedrarag tribe) is one of the places in Laâyoune that carries the name of a historic Sahrawi community. The Oulad Tidrarin are an old Arab-origin Sahrawi tribe long present in the Saguia el-Hamra region.
overview.p2: Rather than a monumental tourist square, it is a living local space – a place of everyday meetings, neighbourhood life and quiet continuity of Sahrawi identity within the modern city.
overview.p3: A short stop here adds depth to a city walk and helps visitors understand that Laâyoune is not only administrative avenues but also the layered presence of its tribal and cultural roots.

food.title: Nearby Food
food.p1: This is primarily a residential and local area rather than a restaurant zone.
food.li1: Small local shops and simple eateries may be found nearby.
food.li2: For a wider choice, return to the cafés and restaurants around Place Mechouar.
food.li3: Street grills and bakeries in central districts are a short taxi or walk away.
food.li4: Traditional Sahrawi tea is easily found in the main café areas of the city.
food.li5: Combine with a meal after exploring the central monuments and markets.
food.p2: The interest of this stop is cultural and atmospheric rather than gastronomic.

1.title: Respect Local Life
1.desc: This is a lived neighbourhood space. Be discreet with photography, especially of people, and move with the same courtesy you would in any residential area.

2.title: Getting There
2.desc: Easily reached by petit taxi from the centre. Ask for Place Oulad Tedrarag or the corresponding neighbourhood name used locally.

3.title: Context Helps
3.desc: A short conversation with a local guide or resident can add meaning – the name connects to the Oulad Tidrarin, one of the historic Sahrawi tribes of the region.

q1.question: Is Place Oulad Tedrarag a major tourist attraction?
q1.answer: No. It is a local square and neighbourhood area linked to Sahrawi heritage. It rewards visitors interested in the lived city rather than monumental sights.

q2.question: Who are the Oulad Tidrarin?
q2.answer: The Oulad Tidrarin (also spelled Oulad Tedrarag / Tidrarine) are a historic Sahrawi tribe of Arab origin long present in the Saguia el-Hamra region.

q3.question: Is it free to visit?
q3.answer: Yes. It is a public local space.

q4.question: How much time should I spend there?
q4.answer: 45 to 90 minutes is enough for a respectful look around and a sense of the neighbourhood atmosphere.

q5.question: Can I combine it with other sites?
q5.answer: Yes. It fits well into a broader city walk that includes Place Mechouar, the Spanish Quarter and the central markets.
